newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission adopts new steel aid rules.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission adopts new steel aid rules.

text.p: The European Commission adopted new rules on Wednesday to control state support to the European Union's steel industry.
The Steel Aid Code will take effect on January 1 next year and be in place until July, 2002.

"The new rules stipulate that member states may grant aid to steel companies only for research and development, environmental protection and full or partial closures of capacities," the Commission said in a statement.
A special provision allows Greece to grant up to 50 million European currency units ($62 million) for the restructuring of its steel firms up until the end of 2000.
EU industry ministers agreed the new code on November 14, after the original Commission proposal had been modified.
Britain, Denmark, Sweden and the Netherlands opposed the original proposal fearing the new code would weaken the rules on when governments could give support to ailing firms.
The current state aid code expires on December 31.
The rules on aid to the steel sector, which ban most state support, are now generally tougher than those for other EU industries.

Among other things, the Commision proposal -- which was modified by ministers -- was intended to put the steel industry, still covered by the 1951 European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) Treaty, on the same footing as other sectors when it comes to research and environmental protection aid.
A further innovation allows closure aid for "partial closures", for example the shutting down of one of a group's plants, as long as there is a reduction in overall capacity. ($1=0.807 Ecu)
